purpose: Define a read-only objective tracker contract without mutating a widget asset or creating a second progression authority.

authority.persistence: FMelodiaNarrativeRecord through the canonical JRPG save contract
forbidden: direct writes to FMelodiaNarrativeRecord from presentation
hardcoded map names, battle IDs, or dialogue logic in the widget
duplicate reward or consequence emission from a tracker refresh

materialization.safe_next_step: Create or adapt one tracker widget that consumes the read model, then compile, save, re-read, and prove restore in PIE.

completion_feedback.trigger: state transition observed from active to completed or failed
completion_feedback.replay_after_restore: presentation may replay a non-mutating summary; it must not reapply the transition

route_marker.missing_marker: show objective text and remain usable without inventing a map or actor reference

restore.behavior: recompute the same read model after map travel, save/load, or process restart

presentation_requirements.requirement: Show exactly one current active objective for the active quest, or a stable terminal summary when no objective is active.
Show optional ordered sub-objectives from the package; do not infer order from widget hierarchy.
Show completion or failure feedback once per observed state transition and allow a harmless replay after restore.
Request a marker by stable package ID and degrade to text when the route resolver is unavailable.
After travel or process restart, read the canonical record again and reproduce the same objective state without emitting gameplay intents.
Expose objective text, state, and completion feedback without relying on color or distortion alone.

offline: Every referenced objective, quest, beat, and route marker resolves in the progression package.
The tracker contract declares no write operation and no widget-owned persistence field.
The current objective is selected from ordered canonical state, not from map name or widget order.

live.assertion: One editor owner materializes the tracker and proves compile/save/readback.
PIE shows active, completion, failure, and restore states without duplicate intent or reward emission.
